latest_release.name: v1.21.1
latest_release.body:
## v1.21.1 — November 9, 2026

This release raises the minimum `follow-redirects` version to fix a published CVE, fixes a Next.js prerendering failure caused by the response duration timer, corrects the `getAdapter` typings, and includes documentation corrections, new test coverage, CI runner changes and dependency updates.

## 🔒 Security Fixes

* **follow-redirects:** Raised the `follow-redirects` range from `^1.16.0` to `^1.16.2` to fix CVE-2026-116689 (GHSA-mrwp-f3q8-3g9p). In the vulnerable versions, `sensitiveHeaders` arrays from another realm were ignored and custom credentials could follow redirects. Only the Node.js HTTP adapter is affected, and there are no API changes. (__#11410__)

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

* **Response Duration:** `dispatchRequest` now measures `response.duration` with `performance.now()` and uses `Date.now()` only when `performance.now()` isn't available. In v1.21.0, any axios request from a Server Component failed Next.js production builds with Cache Components (`cacheComponents: true`), because Next.js rejects `Date.now()` while prerendering. The duration is still a whole number of milliseconds, and system clock changes no longer affect it. (__#11411__)
* **TypeScript:** `getAdapter` now accepts an optional `config?: AxiosRequestConfig` in `index.d.ts` and `index.d.cts`, matching what it does at runtime. You can now call `getAdapter('fetch', { env: { fetch: myFetch } })` without a cast. (__#11404__)

## 🔧 Maintenance & Chores

* **Documentation Corrections:** Brought the README and docs site in line with how axios actually behaves:
  * `transformRequest` runs for every method, and transformers receive `(data, headers, status)`.
  * `responseType` and `Content-Type` have no default value.
  * `AxiosHeaders#get` and `#normalize` are described correctly.
  * Errors should be identified with `axios.isAxiosError()`, not by `name`.
  * The error tables now list `ECONNREFUSED` and `ERR_FORM_DATA_DEPTH_EXCEEDED`, and note that FormData parsing has a fixed depth limit that `maxDepth` doesn't change.
  * New notes cover what `redact` doesn't scan, which adapters enforce `maxContentLength` / `maxBodyLength`, and how `formToJSON()` handles field name collisions.

  (__#11374__, __#11373__, __#11389__, __#11419__, __#11429__, __#11430__)
* **Docs Site:** Added a Partners page, a shared card design for sponsors and partners, a Namespace sponsor badge, and a blog whose first post announces HeroDevs Never-Ending Support for Axios v0. Also applied the v1.20.0/v1.21.0 release notes to the docs, and fixed internal links in the es, fr and zh translations so they keep their locale prefix. (__#11390__, __#11399__, __#11400__, __#11412__, __#11401__)
* **Test Coverage:** Added cancellation tests across the HTTP, fetch and XHR adapters. They cover `AbortSignal`, `CancelToken`, cancelling while a request interceptor is pending, and timeout precedence. Also added tests for `no_proxy` edge cases in `shouldBypassProxy`, such as internationalized domain names, malformed CIDR and IPv4 entries, and port-qualified entries. Neither changes runtime behavior. (__#11376__, __#11431__)
* **CI:** GitHub Actions jobs now run on Namespace runners. The npm publish job stays on GitHub-hosted runners, because npm provenance and trusted publishing (OIDC) only work there. (__#11396__)
* **Dependencies:** Updated development and tooling dependencies, including `vitest` and `@vitest/*` (to 5.x at the root), `typescript` (7.x at the root), `vite`, `rollup`, `eslint`, `playwright`, `@commitlint/*`, `@rollup/plugin-alias`, `@rollup/plugin-terser`, `body-parser`, `multer`, `serialize-javascript`, `fast-uri`, `qs`, `zizmorcore/zizmor-action`, and `follow-redirects` in `/docs`. (__#11383__, __#11375__, __#11372__, __#11345__, __#11392__, __#11387__, __#11386__, __#11385__, __#11391__, __#11388__, __#11395__, __#11421__, __#11422__, __#11426__)
* **Release:** Prepared the 1.21.1 release. (__#11435__)
